\section*{Chapter List}

Status: \yes~written \quad $\circ$~planned. For Part~I the \emph{solved} problems of every pattern are listed; every problem appears in exactly \textbf{one} place in the book, and no problem used here is used in any of the nine companion books (array, binary search, bit, DP, graph, tree, string, recursion, stack--queue--heap).

\subsection*{Part I --- Foundations (Beginner $\to$ CF 1600)}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}c c >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.6cm} X@{}}
\toprule
& \textbf{Ch} & \textbf{Title} & \textbf{Patterns (solved problems)} \\
\midrule
$\circ$ & 1 & Introduction to Greedy Algorithms & Take the best available (Assign Cookies, Maximum Units on a Truck) $\cdot$ Greedy with a running state (Lemonade Change, Minimum Cost of Buying Candies With Discount) $\cdot$ Greedy grouping and counting (Taxi, Maximum Ice Cream Bars) \\
$\circ$ & 2 & First Proofs: Stays Ahead and Exchange & Greedy stays ahead (Maximize Sum Of Array After K Negations, Maximum Element After Decreasing and Rearranging) $\cdot$ Exchange arguments (Minimum Increment to Make Array Unique, Minimum Deletions to Make Character Frequencies Unique) $\cdot$ Local repairs (Minimum Time to Make Rope Colorful, Minimum Replacements to Sort the Array) \\
$\circ$ & 3 & Sorting-Based Greedy & Sort by one key (Advantage Shuffle, Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone) $\cdot$ Sort by a difference or position (Two City Scheduling, Maximum Number of Coins You Can Get) \\
$\circ$ & 4 & Interval Greedy & Stabbing intervals with points (Set Intersection Size At Least Two, Minimum Time to Complete All Tasks) $\cdot$ Events and groups (Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended, Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups) \\
$\circ$ & 5 & Greedy on Numbers and Digits & Digit swaps (Maximum Swap, Previous Permutation With One Swap) $\cdot$ Digit rewrites (Maximum 69 Number, Monotone Increasing Digits) \\
$\circ$ & 6 & Greedy on Strings & Lexicographic choices (Break a Palindrome, Lexicographically Smallest Palindrome) $\cdot$ Building strings under constraints (String Without AAA or BBB, Using a Robot to Print the Lexicographically Smallest String) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
